patients.summary: Retired accountant in Westhampton with HTN, T2DM, HLD and CKD 3 who joined in 2019, had stage I right colon cancer resected in 2020, then hypertensive retinopathy, a conduction block, spinal stenosis, Paget disease, giant cell arteritis and acute pancreatitis. Last seen May 2026 for rapid cognitive decline that outside neurology diagnosed as sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: William Wells, wants to transfer care. Says his old doctor in town is cutting back hours and his wife's friend recommended us. On Medicare, has supplement card. Diabetes and blood pressure, sees nobody else regularly right now.
Booked new patient visit 9/17 at 9:00 with PCP. Release signed by pt over portal for prior PCP records; request faxed today.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
41 pages received from prior PCP office (internal medicine, Hampshire County). Covers 2011 to 2019.
Problem list on their records: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 3.
Med list: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Screening: colonoscopy 2008 reported normal, no polyps. Pneumococcal polysaccharide noted 2018. No Tdap date found.
Filed to media tab. Flagged for PCP before new patient visit.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

66 y/o retired accountant here to transfer primary care. Chronic issues: HTN for many years, type 2 DM roughly a decade, high cholesterol, and stage 3 CKD that his old PCP followed with labs. Feels fine. No chest pain, no breathing trouble with yard work, no foot sores. Takes his pills from a weekly organizer his wife set up.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FH: father had high blood pressure and coronary disease. Mother had type 2 diabetes. A paternal uncle had colon cancer in his seventies.
SH: married, lives in Westhampton. Retired from accounting. Never smoker. Does not drink.

Prior records reviewed: last colonoscopy 2008, normal. Overdue.

Exam: Well appearing. BP and vitals as recorded. Height 178 cm. Fundi not well seen through undilated pupils. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+ both sides. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypertension: at goal on lisinopril + amlodipine. Continue.
2. Type 2 diabetes: on metformin. A1c, urine microalbumin today.
3. CKD 3a: creatinine per old records in the 1.3-1.4 range. Recheck CMP. Avoid NSAIDs, explained.
4. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
5. Health maintenance: Tdap today. Hep C screen today. Colonoscopy referral to GI given the 11-year gap and uncle's history. He would rather not go before the holidays; will let GI call him.
Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Wells, your bloodwork is back. Kidney function is about where your old office had it, stable stage 3. Sugar control (A1c) is good. Cholesterol on atorvastatin is fine. Hepatitis C screen negative, urine protein normal. No changes. See you in December.

procedures.procedure: Colonoscopy with biopsy

documents.title: Colonoscopy report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY — COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Date of procedure: 06/10/2020
Indication: screening, last exam 2008; second-degree relative with colon cancer.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good.
Findings: cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified. In the ascending colon, an irregular partly circumferential mass about 3 cm, friable, non-obstructing; multiple cold forceps biopsies taken and the site tattooed distally. Remainder of colon to rectum normal. No other polyps. Retroflexion normal.
Impression: ascending colon mass, suspicious for malignancy. Pathology pending; patient and wife informed today. Will contact referring PCP with results.
Medications/allergies reviewed: NKDA.

documents.title: Pathology, ascending colon biopsies (outside)
documents.author: pathology
documents.body:
Specimen: ascending colon mass, biopsies.
Diagnosis: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.
Mismatch repair proteins: intact expression (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6).

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mr. Wells with his wife on speaker. Biopsy shows colon cancer. GI had already told them it looked suspicious so not a total surprise, but hard to hear. Answered questions as best I could. Next steps: staging CT scans and CEA, then surgical consult. Referrals placed urgently to general surgery and oncology. GI is ordering the CTs. Will call him after scans. He has my cell through the practice line if he needs it.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast. Indication: staging, colon adenocarcinoma. Lungs clear without nodule or mass. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart normal in size. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of metastatic disease in the chest.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Reduced-volume IV contrast given for renal function. Mild wall thickening in the ascending colon at the known tumor site with a tattoo marker distally; no pericolonic stranding. No enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal nodes. Liver without focal lesion. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenals normal. Kidneys normal in size, no hydronephrosis. No ascites. Bladder and prostate unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Known ascending colon primary. No lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis.

documents.title: CT staging (outside)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: See attached reports. CEA drawn same morning: within normal limits.

reports.text: Right colon and terminal ileum, resection: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, 3.1 cm, ascending colon. Tumor invades into the muscularis propria. No lymphovascular invasion identified. Proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Nineteen lymph nodes examined, all negative.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of ascending colon, pT2 N0, margins negative.

procedures.procedure: Right hemicolectomy

documents.title: Discharge summary (outside hospital)
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/08/2020, discharged 07/11/2020.
Procedure 07/08: laparoscopic-assisted right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis for ascending colon adenocarcinoma.
Course: uncomplicated. Diet advanced day 2, bowel function by day 3. Metformin held while NPO and resumed on discharge. Discharge home with wife.
Final pathology: adenocarcinoma invading the muscularis propria (pT2), 0 of 19 lymph nodes involved (pN0), margins negative. AJCC stage I.
Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; medical oncology to discuss surveillance.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, two weeks after right hemicolectomy. Saw surgery yesterday, incisions healing, they were happy.
Eating normally, bowels loose for a week then settling. Pain mostly gone. Back on all his regular meds including metformin. Sugars not checked.
Path reviewed: stage I, nodes negative. He was relieved.
Oncology appointment in August.
Plan: no changes. BMP when he is out for his oncology visit or at next in-person.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — CONSULT LETTER
Seen 08/05/2020 for stage I (pT2 N0) adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy 07/08/2020. MMR proficient. Pre-op CEA normal; staging CTs without metastasis.
He is recovering well. Exam unremarkable, incisions healed.
Recommendation: no adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated for stage I disease. Surveillance: clinic visit with CEA yearly, colonoscopy at one year from surgery.
Family history reviewed: no first-degree relative with colorectal cancer; a paternal uncle had colon cancer in his 70s.
Thank you for this referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person for the first time since his surgery. Feels back to normal, walking 2 miles. Appetite good, weight down a few pounds and now stable.
Oncology: no chemo, yearly visits, colonoscopy next summer. Updated problem list to history of colon cancer.
BP fine at home. No hypoglycemia symptoms.
Exam: abdomen with healed laparoscopic incisions, soft, nontender. Heart and lungs normal. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good.
Plan: A1c, BMP, lipids today. Continue meds. Flu shot in October with nurse.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 06/30/2021
Mr. Wells, 68, returns a year out from his right hemicolectomy for stage I colon adenocarcinoma. He has had no new symptoms and says he has felt well since the operation.
Other history: hypertension (lisinopril, amlodipine), type 2 diabetes (metformin), hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 3. Meds also atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Never smoker, no alcohol. Retired accountant. No colorectal cancer in a first-degree relative.
Vitals normal. Exam: unremarkable, no adenopathy, abdomen benign.
Labs: Hgb 13.8, WBC 7.2, platelets 250. Na 140, K 4.2, fasting glucose 98. CEA within normal limits.
Assessment: no evidence of recurrence. Plan: surveillance colonoscopy due now (GI arranging), annual visit and CEA.

orders.reason: abnormal vision screen, diabetic eye exam

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV plus chronic f/u.
Vision: for several months notices his side vision isn't as sharp and lights at night have a fuzzy halo. No sudden change, no eye pain. Never needed glasses. Last eye exam he can't remember, years.
Snellen today reduced both eyes compared with what he expected (see vitals flowsheet). No other new issues.
PHQ-2 negative. No falls. Independent.
Exam: undilated fundi poorly seen. Otherwise normal. Feet intact.
A/P
1. Abnormal vision screen with peripheral vision complaints: ophthalmology referral for dilated exam; also due for diabetic eye exam.
2. DM/HTN/CKD: labs today.
3. Prevention: pneumococcal conjugate next visit.

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation (outside)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY
Visit 01/05/2022. Referred for an abnormal vision screen.
69-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD and a history of colon cancer. No acute loss of vision. Over several months he has noticed occasional trouble with peripheral vision and a fuzziness around bright lights. Does not wear corrective lenses. He admits he has not always been consistent with his blood pressure medication.
Meds per patient list; NKDA. Nonsmoker, no alcohol.
Exam: visual acuity mildly reduced in both eyes. Intraocular pressures normal. Dilated fundus exam: arteriovenous nicking of the retinal vessels. No diabetic retinopathy seen.
Impression: hypertensive retinopathy.
Plan: blood pressure control is the treatment; discussed taking his pills daily. Return 1 year, sooner for any change.

documents.title: Re: eye doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Eye doctor said the blood vessels in back of my eyes show the blood pressure. I'll be honest I miss the evening pills sometimes. Should I change anything?

documents.title: Re: eye doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for being straight with me. Your BP pills are both once a day, so you can take them together in the morning with the metformin. That alone might fix it. Keep a few home readings and bring them in March.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Moved both BP meds to mornings after the eye visit; says he hasn't missed since. Home log 124-136 / 74-82.
Hypertensive retinopathy noted on Jan eye exam. No diabetic retinopathy.
No complaints today.
Exam: as charted. RRR, lungs clear, no edema.
Plan: continue. BMP and A1c today. PCV in the fall with flu. RTC 6 mo.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Asked to be seen: for a few months, every couple of weeks, a brief lightheaded feeling, seconds, usually sitting or standing around, not with exertion. Never passed out, no chest pain, no racing heart. Not tied to meals. Sugars not low as far as he knows.
Meds unchanged, taking them all in the morning now.
Exam: BP as charted, orthostatic readings without a drop. HR regular. No murmur, no carotid bruit. Neuro nonfocal.
A/P: intermittent lightheadedness without syncope. BP not low. Will ask cardiology to evaluate with rhythm assessment given age and diabetes. Told him not to drive if he feels faint and to call 911 for passing out or chest pain.

conditions.label: First-degree AV block with bundle branch block (incomplete trifascicular block)

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. First-degree AV block, PR 220 ms. QRS duration 120 ms with bundle branch block.
reports.conclusion: First-degree AV block with bundle branch block.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation (outside)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP — CONSULT
Date of visit 07/07/2022. Reason: lightheadedness.
69M, history of colon cancer s/p resection, hypertensive retinopathy, HTN, DM2, HLD, CKD 3. Overall feels well; occasional lightheaded episodes over a few months. No chest pain, palpitations or syncope.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, amlodipine 5, aspirin 81. NKDA.
FH: father HTN and CAD. Never smoker, no alcohol, retired accountant.
Exam: BP 132/78, HR 58 and regular. Heart sounds without murmur, rub or gallop.
ECG: sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block with PR 220 ms; QRS 120 ms with bundle branch block.
Impression: first-degree AV block with bundle branch block (incomplete trifascicular block). No pacing indication at present.
Plan: avoid beta-blockers, nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers and other AV-nodal slowing drugs. Call or go to the ED for any fainting. Annual ECG here.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cardiology letter reviewed: first-degree AV block plus bundle branch block, no pacemaker now, avoid AV nodal blockers. Added an alert to the chart. He still gets the odd lightheaded second or two, no worse. No fainting.
BP good. Diabetes stable.
Exam: RRR, slow-normal rate. Lungs clear. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable.
Plan: PCV20 today (prior PPSV23 2018). Labs today. RTC after AWV.

events.reason: Back and leg pain with walking

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: low back and bilateral leg pain with walking

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
For about four months, low back ache and both legs ache when he walks more than a few minutes. Better when he sits, or leans on the cart at the grocery store. No numbness, tingling, weakness. No bowel or bladder trouble. No fever, no weight loss.
Exam: tender to lumbar extension, flexion fine. Straight leg raise negative. Strength 5/5, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact. Pedal pulses palpable.
A/P: story sounds like spinal stenosis (neurogenic claudication), though vascular claudication should be excluded given DM. Orthopedics referral; they can check ABI. No NSAIDs with his kidneys.

documents.title: Orthopedic spine note (outside)
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDICS — brief note to PCP (visit 07/10/2023)
70M with six months of low back pain and bilateral leg pain, a dull ache that comes on after a few minutes of walking and eases with sitting or bending forward; no numbness or tingling. Lumbar extension provokes pain. Sensation and motor strength intact in both legs. ABI normal.
Impression: lumbar spinal stenosis. Plan: MRI lumbar spine, physical therapy referral, follow up as needed.

documents.title: Saw the back doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw orthopedics Monday. He thinks it's narrowing in the lower spine, not my circulation, they did the leg pressure test and it was normal. MRI ordered and physical therapy. Just letting you know since we haven't gotten a letter.

documents.title: Re: Saw the back doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks, that fits. Good that the leg circulation test was normal. I'll watch for the MRI.

reports.text: Five lumbar-type vertebrae. Alignment normal. Vertebral body heights preserved; no fracture or marrow lesion. Conus normal, ends at L1. L3-L4: disc bulge and facet hypertrophy with mild central canal narrowing. L4-L5: disc bulge with facet arthropathy and ligamentum flavum thickening producing moderate central canal stenosis; foramina adequately patent. L5-S1: no significant narrowing.
reports.conclusion: Moderate central canal stenosis at L4-L5; mild at L3-L4.

documents.title: MRI lumbar spine (outside)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outside report received, see results.

DM/HTN: no issues.
Exam: gait normal. No edema.
Plan: continue home exercises. Flu/COVID/RSV with nurse in October. RTC AWV.

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Different from the back: for about a year, a deep ache in the left hip and upper thigh, worse as the day goes on, makes him stop and rest walking the neighborhood loop. Wife came today and adds that his hat doesn't fit anymore (bought a bigger one) and he has the TV louder for months. No fever, chills, sweats, weight loss, no fall or injury.
Exam: mild frontal prominence of the forehead. Hearing reduced to whisper on the left. Left thigh appears slightly bowed. Hip ROM mildly painful at end range. Neuro intact.
A/P: thigh pain, skull change, hearing loss — concern for Paget disease of bone. CMP today (alk phos). Will refer to endocrinology depending on result.

orders.reason: elevated alkaline phosphatase, suspected Paget disease

documents.title: Blood test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Wells, your alkaline phosphatase (a bone/liver enzyme) is high while calcium and liver tests are normal. Together with the thigh, hat size and hearing, Paget disease of bone is the likely cause. I've referred you to endocrinology, who treat this. It is very treatable. Kidney numbers stable.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation (outside)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY
Seen 06/28/2024 at your request.
71-year-old with HTN, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, colon cancer treated by resection, and lumbar stenosis. Walking has become harder over the past year with a deep left hip and upper thigh ache that builds through the day; he stops frequently on neighborhood walks. Hat size has gone up recently and his wife notes months of poor hearing. No fevers, chills, night sweats, weight loss or trauma. Lives independently, retired from accounting.
Exam: T 36.7, BP 142/86, BMI 26. Mild frontal bossing; hearing decreased on the left; bowing deformity of the left femur. Neurologic exam normal.
Labs: calcium normal, phosphate normal, alkaline phosphatase elevated.
Impression: Paget disease of bone.
Plan: skull, pelvis and left femur radiographs; 25-OH vitamin D; then zoledronic acid infusion if vitamin D adequate. Renal function acceptable for a single 5 mg dose with hydration.

Zoledronic acid 5 mg IV given 07/30/2024 in our infusion suite with pre-hydration; tolerated with one day of achiness. Recheck alkaline phosphatase in 6 months.

Routine. Feels well. Endo says Paget's labs normalized.
Labs today show creatinine 1.8, eGFR now under 45 — restaging CKD to 3b. Potassium fine, urine albumin normal.
Discussed: keep BP controlled, avoid NSAIDs, contrast caution.
Exam: unremarkable.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — visit 07/05/2025
72M with hypertensive retinopathy and Paget disease. Two hours ago, while reading, a shadow came down over the vision of his right eye. Painless, no improvement since. Several weeks of mild fatigue and general aching, did not seek care. No trauma, no double vision, no discharge.
Vitals: T 37.8 C, P 78, BP 136/72, RR 16.
Exam: tender right temple with diminished temporal pulse. Reports jaw discomfort when chewing.
Labs: ESR 88 mm/h, CRP 74 mg/L.
Impression: giant cell arteritis with right eye vision loss.
Treatment: prednisone 60 mg daily started in the ED. Ophthalmology contacted; temporal artery biopsy scheduled this week. Discharged with close follow-up. PCP to follow sugars on steroids.
Allergies: NKDA.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen Saturday in the ED with sudden right-eye vision loss, temple tenderness, jaw pain, high ESR/CRP — giant cell arteritis. On prednisone 60 mg daily since Saturday. Biopsy Thursday. Ophthalmology following the eye. Headache and jaw better already; fatigue persists. Wife driving him.
Sugars: borrowed his neighbor's meter, fasting readings 160s-180s.
Exam: right temple mildly tender. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P
1. GCA on high-dose prednisone: rheumatology referral to manage taper. Biopsy 7/10.
2. Steroid hyperglycemia: will get him a meter and strips, check fasting and pre-supper. Continue metformin. Call if >300.
3. HTN, CKD: BMP today.

reports.text: Right temporal artery, biopsy, 2.2 cm segment. Transmural granulomatous inflammation centered on the media with multinucleated giant cells and fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina; intimal thickening.

documents.title: Temporal artery biopsy pathology (outside)
documents.author: pathology
documents.body: Outside pathology report received; see result.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation (outside)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Seen 08/05/2025. Biopsy-proven giant cell arteritis with right eye involvement in July. Symptoms resolved on prednisone 60 mg. Reducing to 40 mg daily now, then gradual taper over the coming months per our schedule. Will see every 6-8 weeks. Glucose monitoring by PCP appreciated.

documents.title: Sugar numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Fasting 150s and before supper as high as 240 since the prednisone. Rheumatology lowered me to 40. Is this okay or do I need something?

documents.title: Re: Sugar numbers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those are what we expect on this much prednisone and they should come down as the dose goes down. Nothing over 300, so no change for now. Keep logging and send me numbers in 3 weeks or sooner if over 300.

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED — 11/02/2025
73-year-old man, HTN, DM2, CKD and recent giant cell arteritis, with 12 hours of sudden, severe, sharp upper abdominal pain going through to his back. Had a cardiac catheterization two weeks ago to evaluate chest pain.
Meds listed: aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 5. NKDA.
VS: BP 150/90, HR 98, T 37.2.
Exam: epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding, bowel sounds present, no jaundice, no ascites. Bluish toes; lacy violaceous mottling of the skin of both legs.
Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250. Amylase 800, lipase 900. Creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.8). AST 45, ALT 50, T bili 1.2.
Dx: acute pancreatitis. IV fluids, analgesia, antiemetic. Admitted to medicine.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (20 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 11/2 with acute pancreatitis (lipase 900), admitted three nights per patient; discharge summary not yet received. Back to eating normally before discharge, no pain now. No alcohol ever.
Also learned today: in late October he had a cardiac catheterization through his cardiologist after some chest pain. He says no stent was placed and no medicines were changed. No chest pain since. We don't have that report.
Prednisone: rheumatology has him at 20 mg daily now.
Exam: abdomen soft, nontender. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
A/P
1. Acute pancreatitis, resolved clinically. CMP, CBC, lipase today.
2. Cardiac cath: request report from cardiology.
3. GCA on prednisone 20, per rheumatology. A1c today.
4. CKD 3b: creatinine 2.1 in ED; recheck today.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed request to outside cardiology group for cath report (approx 10/20/25) and last office note, and to hospital for 11/2-11/5 discharge summary. Will follow up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs after the hospital: lipase back to normal, kidney number improving toward your usual, A1c higher from the prednisone as expected. No changes.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's wife called to cancel tomorrow's AWV, he is worn out after a rheumatology appointment and a busy week. Will rebook after the holidays.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up (outside)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Visit 01/13/2026: no headache, jaw pain or new visual symptoms. Inflammatory markers normal. Prednisone reduced to 10 mg daily; continuing slow taper.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (10 mg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked visit. On prednisone 10 mg now. Sugars lower than in the fall, fasting 120s-140s.
Cardiology report and hospital summary still not received despite request; re-sent.
No abdominal pain since November.
Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet ok.
A1c drawn today; expect it to stay up while on prednisone and drift down after. Continue metformin.
RTC May.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chronic f/u, wife present. She asked to speak first: over the past several weeks he repeats questions, forgets conversations from the same day, and got muddled doing the household bills, which he has done for 40 years. Some confusion about the day. He thinks she's overstating it but agrees he is "foggy."
No headache, jaw pain or vision change. No falls. Prednisone now 5 mg per rheumatology.
Exam: alert, pleasant, but vague on recent events. Cognitive screen today: missed delayed recall items, clock drawing disorganized. Speech fluent. No focal weakness. Gait normal.
A/P
1. New cognitive decline over weeks, faster than typical. Labs today: CBC, CMP, B12, TSH. Urgent neurology referral. Wife to drive; he agreed to stop driving for now.
2. GCA: prednisone 5 mg, rheumatology managing.
3. DM/HTN/CKD: A1c today. BP a bit above goal today; home readings have been fine, no change.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mrs. Wells, writing to you both as discussed. Blood counts, B12, thyroid and chemistry are normal; kidney number is at his usual. A1c 7.2, better. Nothing in the blood explains the memory change, so the neurology visit is the next step. The referral went out marked urgent.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: neurology appointment is 7/3, earliest they had. She feels he is a bit worse, more confused in the evenings, but safe at home and eating. No falls, no fever. Advised she can call neurology for cancellation list; ED if sudden change, weakness or fall. PCP aware.

documents.title: Neurology consultation (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — visit 07/03/2026
73-year-old man with a history of colon cancer and giant cell arteritis, seen with his wife for about three months of quickly worsening memory loss, confusion and sudden jerking movements. She says the decline has accelerated in the past month and he now sometimes does not recognize family members.
Meds per wife: metformin, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Exam: disoriented, has difficulty following commands. Myoclonic jerks of both upper extremities.
Routine blood work normal.
MRI brain: diffuse cortical atrophy; no stroke or mass.
EEG: sharp, triphasic, synchronous discharges.
Impression: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Lumbar puncture for CSF studies being arranged. Discussed with his wife at length.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Lumbar puncture 07/14/2026. CSF RT-QuIC positive, consistent with sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Results reviewed with Mrs. Wells on 08/07. Care is supportive. We discussed palliative care involvement and support at home; she will speak with his primary care physician. Infection control guidance for any future procedures given. Neurology will continue to follow.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mrs. Wells called after the neurology results. Wants to sit down with PCP about care at home and what help is available. He is home, eating with help, sleeping more. Booked 9/1 at 2:00, 40 minutes. PCP to call her before then.

documents.title: PCP call back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Mrs. Wells. Sorry for this news. Talked through what the visit on 9/1 can cover. She has the neurology letter. She'll bring his pill bottles and the health care proxy form.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: metformin and atorvastatin 90-day. Sent per protocol; PCP to review all meds at 9/1 visit.
